payload.author: andyengit
payload.body:
I am referring to https://github.com/OCA/l10n-venezuela/pull/39 and https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/156429

At the time this was intended for 16.0. I am now targeting 17.0 so it can be forward-ported to newer versions.

The goal is:

Update the chart of accounts (I am not sure whether this should be a new chart, specifically on master @pedrobaeza ).
Update the taxes.

payload.author: pedrobaeza
payload.body:
I think it's reasonable to fix it for stable versions, as anyway the current CoA is not usable in Venezuela. Perhaps 17.0, being about to been dropped from support, is too old, but 18.0 for sure.

Let's see what @jco-odoo thinks about this. Are you the one also maintaining these CoA, Josse?

payload.author: bwealthics
payload.body:
Hi @andyengit, first the disclosure: I opened #285503, which proposes a
6-digit VEN-NIF plan as an *additional* template on master rather than a
replacement. It is meant as an answer to the question you raise above ("I am
not sure whether this should be a new chart"), not as a competing proposal.
If the conclusion here is that one replaced chart is the right call, I will
close mine.

That said, here is something concrete for this PR, since `ci/l10n` is red and
fails after 3 seconds.

None of the 133 accounts in the new `account.account-ve.csv` is typed
`equity_unaffected`. Odoo needs exactly one to link the current year result to
the balance sheet, and a chart template without it does not load cleanly. The
natural candidate is already in the plan:

    "account_account_3101006","UTILIDADES DEL EJERCICIO","3101006","equity","False"

Changing that one `equity` to `equity_unaffected` is likely all that is needed.
Worth noting the old `ve` chart had the same gap, so this is inherited, not
introduced by you.

Three smaller things I noticed while reading the CSV:

* `3101003 CAPITAL SUSCRITO POR COPBAR` still carries a company name. It is
  the same class of leftover as the `MARKETING COMPANY ...` accounts this PR
  is removing, so it would be a shame to keep it.
* `1107004 I.S.L.R. RETENIDO` and `1107005 I.V.A. RETENIDO` are in class 1 but
  typed `liability_current`. As withholdings suffered they are tax credits,
  so `asset_current` looks right.
* Three accounts share the name `ACTUALIZACION DEL VALOR` (`3101002`,
  `3101013`, `3101015`), and `GASTOS DE REPRESENTACION` appears twice
  (`5102012`, `6101004`). Users will not be able to tell them apart in the
  account picker.

Happy to help with any of this. Getting a correct Venezuelan chart into the
core is worth more than which of the two proposals gets there.

payload.author: vchu-odoo
payload.body:
Hello,
Thank you for the fix!

Can not we solve it by fixing the `write` override?
I believe that the issue is that we fallback on `order.partner_id` address when we switch from pick up in store and we do not update delivery methods on country change.
Or we may just need to reload the page once we switch from the pickup in store...

payload.author: TudorCalinCS
payload.body:
Hello @vchu-odoo, thanks for the suggestion! I tried both locally.

Changing `write()` alone does not work. `/shop/set_delivery_method` only continues if the method is in `_get_delivery_methods()`, and that still matches the pickup address. The country-specific method is rejected, `carrier_id` is never written, and the fallback to `partner_id` never runs.

Reloading alone does not work either. The order is still on pick up in store, so the reload still uses the pickup country: the address looks unselected and the country-specific method disappears until you pick the customer address again.

However, they work when combined: write the new carrier first so that `write()` can restore the customer address, then reload the page to rebuild the delivery method list. The drawbacks are the extra full-page reload and writing `carrier_id` before the method has passed the normal availability and rating flow.

Let me know what you think!

payload.author: seb-odoo
payload.body:
Hello, thanks for writing these down, this is much better than having them live in review comments (and in our heads) only.

One thing bigger than the content: coding_guidelines.rst in odoo/documentation currently prescribes the exact tree 0001 calls bad (static/src/js, static/src/xml, static/src/scss). If this lands we have two official answers, so I think the documentation should be adapted/removed in the same batch.

I tend to prefer having them in the code directly rather than a separate repo. It makes sense that guideline and tips apply to a specific version of the code and evolve with it (mentioning `useEffect` in a generic guideline would be confusing depending on OWL version, for example). Having to maintain a separate repo is a pain, but I know it also has value.

What reads skills/ at the root? Claude discovers skills under .claude/skills/, so as far as I can tell nothing picks this up automatically. But I guess we do want to be harness agnostic and expect devs to point their AI at this folder?

payload.title: [IMP] web: collect garbage between test files on demand

payload.author: aab-odoo
payload.body:
@seb-odoo I already tested a similar approach in the past and it doesn't work. It is actually slower. In 18.0, it's not obvious:
This branch's last build:
> 2026-08-27 10:01:47,330 26 INFO 123104462-18-0-all odoo.addons.web.tests.test_js.WebSuite.test_unit_desktop.browser: [HOOT] Passed 12719 tests (49757 assertions, total time: 00:18:56) 

Last 18.0's build:
> 2026-08-27 09:19:42,822 26 INFO 123100886-18-0-all odoo.addons.web.tests.test_js.WebSuite.test_unit_desktop.browser: [HOOT] Passed 12719 tests (49757 assertions, total time: 00:17:17) 

But you can see it is sligthly slower. You could argue that there's some variance, which is true.

However I tried in master a few months ago, where the suite is 3/4 times longer, and it even reached the timeout: https://runbot.odoo.com/runbot/batch/2588039/build/114368047

My strategy was more naive, as I hardcoded a memory threshold to trigger the gc, but I expect yours to behave similarily.

payload.author: seb-odoo
payload.body:
Thank you for checking it.

I don't think we can draw conclusions from a single build, but if the outcome is not clear yet, I'm ok to investigate deeper whether or not this is worth it.

I can take back the ideas from your diff, at least to keep the log when skipped.

payload.author: seb-odoo
payload.body:
Ok so, basically when we skip a gc, the following one costs proportionally more, pretty much in the same ratio. So we don't gain much over a long test suite. And if we skip them all, chrome collects on its own, and its own ones are worse.

Not exactly the same ratio though, so a threshold gains a bit. Just too little to bother.

We do gain on a very small test suite though, if we just end before we need any gc at all. Which is what I observed initially. Same for a local test run. Or if we time it to end on the biggest memory possible. As the last gc is wasted anyway.

Also we do lose precise memory usage over test files if we skip some. With no collection before it, the garbage is counted in it too.

Considering that, I agree to close.

Hi @FlorianGilbert
You reviewed https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/274312, and this is the same task cherry-picked onto saas-19.3.

On the original PR I commented @robodoo up to saas-19.2 because I wanted the chain to stop there so I could make some changes before continuing. That cap is still in effect, so it is no longer forward-porting on its own and I opened this hop by hand. 

Could you have a look when you get a chance?

payload.author: xmo-odoo
payload.body:
> On the original PR I commented @robodoo up to saas-19.2 because I wanted the chain to stop there so I could make some changes before continuing. That cap is still in effect, so it is no longer forward-porting on its own and I opened this hop by hand.

FWIW the forward port mode does not influence the limit (the mode used to be implemented via the limit but that's not been the case in a long time) so `fw=default` on #284334 was a no-op, it changed the mode from default to default.

You should have been able to resume forward-porting by changing the limit back to master ("up to master"). It's also not really useful to force the forward-porting to stop like that (even less so as in this case there was a conflict so it would have stopped either way), reminding yourself that you wanted to change something is a lot more valuable and there's a mergebot command for that (`remindme`).

payload.author: hahu-odoo
payload.body:
Very interesting; leaving this for visibility:

The way I was able to get back to the state before I messed up the merge conflict (I didn't realize I messed it up) and then immediately amended and force-pushed was like this:

```
$ git reflog
...
ae6a921dd734 (HEAD -> master-saas-19.3-runbot-243064-hahu-560938-fw, dev/master-saas-19.3-runbot-243064-hahu-560938-fw) HEAD@{10}: commit (amend): [FIX] point_of_sale, pos_stock: decouple limited products tests
e8b92decc5f1 HEAD@{11}: checkout: moving from master to master-saas-19.3-runbot-243064-hahu-560938-fw
...
```

I had to use that hash from `HEAD@{11}` which would have had the exact state the branch was in when I checked out this branch from GitHub. Because I amended my original commit, that commit hash was lost (kind of), so I needed to use the hash of the branch state from before I did any amending.

So in summary,
```
$ git reset HEAD~1
$ git cherry-pick e8b92decc5f1
```

payload.title: [PERF] stock: optimize _get_domain_locations_new

payload.author: Aurelienvd
payload.body:
I understand the point of the fix but I find it really situational. Having 300K locations is not the norm, it's a clear outlier. And the fix only makes sense when the HashTable of the Subplan does not fit in memory. Even with PostgreSQL defaults, this is 64Mb x 2 so 128Mb. It's really not that frequent that we would need to manually hint the row estimates.

Also the bad estimation is still there, it's just capped. And I don't know how this is gonna behave in future PostgreSQL versions that might have better planner estimations.

Lastly, in cases where the hashed SubPlan fits in memory, this is doing an additional `search_count` for nothing no ? And this should be the most common case as 300K locations is pretty rare.

In the end I'm not super fan of the fix. But could you share the query plan before/after the fix so we can see what's happening in the query planner ?

payload.author: juwu-odoo
payload.body:
@Aurelienvd 

I meant in the commit message that ~300k total locations is the theoretical max after the change. On the actual benchmark, the hash table was hitting 10MB when querying with 18 resupply locations and 30k total locations.

BUT your point is still right I think, I was testing with the out-of-the-box default of `work_mem=4MB` on my machine which causes the issue. And the client is an on-premise as well so I think they might also have the OOB `work_mem=4MB` too 😅. I'll probably just let them know to increase their `work_mem` to a reasonable amount like 64MB which would give them 10x the headroom.

Thanks for the input!

For your reference, if you're still interested:
Plan before: https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/2h8da7118116ee8d
Plan after: https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/372cefgb6f834a82
